contests.title: Norton — Finance and Law Department supervision

provenance.quote:
Shall Article IV, Section 4.03 of the Charter of the City of
Norton, Ohio be changed and amended to place the Department
of Finance and Department of Law under the direct
administrative supervision of the Administrative Officer, while
preserving the existing appointment and removal provisions and
the legally vested fiscal and professional legal duties of those
offices, to read as follows:
SECTION 4.03 POWERS AND DUTIES.
The Administrative Officer shall be responsible to the Mayor for
the proper administration of all areas of government assigned to
him or her by this Charter or by ordinance of Council adopted
pursuant to the Charter. The Administrative Officer shall:
(a) Until Council provides otherwise, serve as Director of Public
Safety, Director of Public Service, and Director of Personnel, and
Director of Economic and Community Development in
accordance with Charter Sections 5.05A, 5.06A and 5.07B.
(b) Direct and supervise the administration and operation of
the Department of Finance and the Department of Law,
including the Director of Finance and the Director of Law.
Such supervision shall not alter or transfer any authority or
procedure established by this Charter with respect to the
appointment, confirmation, suspension, or removal of the
Director of Finance or the Director of Law; shall not transfer
or diminish any power or duty vested by law or this Charter
in the Director of Finance or the Director of Law; and shall
not authorize the Administrative Officer to direct, control, or
interfere with the professional legal judgement, legal
opinions, representation, or professional obligations of the
Director of Law.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews the school district’s 1% tax on residents’ earned income for current school operating expenses for five years beginning January 1, 2028. The existing income tax expires at the end of 2027.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the 1% earned-income tax for five years.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not renew this income tax through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews a property-tax levy for ongoing permanent school improvements for five years, commencing 2027 and first due 2028. The rate is capped at 2 mills per dollar of taxable value; the auditor estimates $244,127 annually and $28 per $100,000 of market value.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the proposed five-year permanent-improvement levy.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not renew this levy through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds a 1% annual tax on earned income of residents of Orrville City School District for current school expenses for five years beginning January 1, 2027.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional 1% earned-income tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not impose this additional income tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds a 0.75% annual tax on earned income of residents of Triway Local School District for current school expenses for three years beginning January 1, 2027.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional 0.75% earned-income tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not impose this additional income tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Places the Finance and Law Departments under the Administrative Officer’s direct administrative supervision. Existing appointment and removal rules and the directors’ legal duties remain in place; the officer cannot direct or interfere with the Law Director’s professional legal judgment.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the supervision change with the stated protections.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter change.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes the title of Norton’s chief legal officer from Solicitor to Director of Law. Appointment, qualifications, powers, duties, suspension and removal rules stay the same.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Change the title to Director of Law.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not make this title change.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Repeals outdated language about employees’ civil-service status when Rittman became a city and adds a section allowing other council members to remove a council member for bad behavior, criminal conduct or absenteeism.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt both the repeal and the new council-removal section.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Moves the annual organizational meeting from the first Monday in December to the year’s first regular meeting, starts elected officials’ terms on January 1 instead of the first Monday in December, and moves the nomination-petition deadline from 75 to 90 days before an election.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt all three charter changes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Rittman City Council to hold executive sessions for any reason permitted by the Ohio Revised Code.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the executive-session provision.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Clarifies that the mayor, when invited to a City Council executive session, attends without presiding.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the clarification of the mayor’s role.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes the charter language describing how a City Council member is nominated to and can become mayor when the mayor’s office is vacant.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the proposed mayoral-vacancy procedure.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires City Council to review the Municipal Manager annually.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Require the annual review.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Updates charter language to reflect the existing merger of the Fire and EMS Departments into one department.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Update the charter references to the combined department.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires the Law Director to be an attorney in good standing with the state bar association and to oversee representation of the city in all cases as well as provide direct representation.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the qualifications and representation requirements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Updates outdated language about establishing a Civil Service Commission if Rittman becomes a city, because Rittman is already a city.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the city-status language update.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Reduces Civil Service Commission members’ terms from six years to three years.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt three-year terms.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds a City Council member to the Cemetery Board.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Add the council member to the board.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Moves the deadline for submitting the budget to City Council from January 1 to December 31 and clarifies the charter language.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the December31 submission deadline and language changes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires City Council to review the Finance Director annually.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Require the annual review.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Reduces the residency requirement for election as a municipal officer from two years to one year.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the one-year residency requirement.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes when the Charter Review Commission convenes so that its schedule does not align with election of new City Council members.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the proposed charter-review schedule.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this charter amendment.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Asks for voters’ nonbinding opinion on whether Village Council should consider zoning rules permitting and regulating short-term rentals in the BD Downtown Business and BG General Business Districts. Approval expresses an opinion; it does not itself adopt zoning rules.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Advise Council to consider the proposed short-term rental zoning rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Advise against considering those zoning rules through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Asks for voters’ nonbinding opinion on whether Village Council should consider zoning rules permitting adult-use marijuana dispensaries in the BD Downtown Business and BG General Business Districts. Approval expresses an opinion; it does not itself adopt zoning rules.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Advise Council to consider zoning rules permitting those dispensaries.
measureRecords.noMeans: Advise against considering those zoning rules through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Repeals Ordinance 2025-4, the village ordinance providing for photo traffic enforcement, which Council enacted March 18, 2025.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Repeal the photo traffic enforcement ordinance.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not repeal the ordinance through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Chooses a commission to draw up proposed conditions for merging the Village of Doylestown and Chippewa Township. The question authorizes preparation of merger terms; it does not itself merge the governments.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Choose a commission to prepare proposed merger conditions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not choose a merger commission through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Chooses a commission to draw up proposed conditions for merging the Village of Doylestown and Chippewa Township. The question authorizes preparation of merger terms; it does not itself merge the governments.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Choose a commission to prepare proposed merger conditions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not choose a merger commission through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews a property-tax levy for township road and bridge construction, reconstruction, resurfacing and repairs for five years, commencing 2026 and first due 2027. The cap is 1.9 mills per dollar of taxable value; the auditor estimates $70,956 annually and $20 per $100,000 of market value.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew this five-year road levy.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not renew this levy through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews a property-tax levy for fire and ambulance protection for four years, commencing 2027 and first due 2028. The cap is 1.5 mills per dollar of taxable value; the auditor estimates $98,495 annually and $30 per $100,000 of market value.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew this four-year fire and ambulance levy.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not renew this levy through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds a property-tax levy to construct, improve or maintain a building for firefighting and emergency medical services for five years, commencing 2026 and first due 2027. The cap is 1.5 mills per dollar of taxable value; the auditor estimates $343,342 annually and $53 per $100,000 of market value.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional five-year building levy.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not impose this additional levy.
